evals.name: precedent-only-justification-challenged
evals.prompt: reason don't recite — you told me to structure the new module the same way as the existing one because "that's how this repo does it." Is that actually the right call?
evals.expected_output: The skill re-anchors the incumbency discipline, names the precedent-only justification as a located finding, and corrects forward by re-deriving from first principles: it states the actual purpose the structure should serve and tests whether copying the existing form serves it — rather than restating that the existing module does it that way.
expectations: Flags 'that's how this repo does it' as a precedent-only justification with no stated rationale
Re-derives from the actual purpose rather than restating the inherited pattern
Reaches a reasoned verdict (confirm with a live rationale, or challenge with an alternative)

evals.name: confirming-inherited-choice-is-valid
evals.prompt: reason don't recite — check the retry policy we inherited. (It exists because the downstream API rate-limits bursts, and the current backoff was tuned against that limit.)
evals.expected_output: Re-derivation confirms the inherited choice: it stands on a live rationale (the documented rate-limit purpose), so the skill reports it clean. It does not treat the challenge as a mandate to overturn a well-justified convention or manufacture dissent.
expectations: Recognizes the inherited choice has a live rationale and confirms it
Does NOT overturn or churn a well-justified convention just because it was interrogated
Reports clean rather than fabricating a first-principles objection

evals.name: standards-disagreement-routes-upstream
evals.prompt: reason don't recite — I think our shared standards doc's rule here is actually wrong for this case. Should I just ignore it?
evals.expected_output: Because the interrogated content is a shared standard, the skill does not endorse silently deviating from it OR silently conforming — it routes the disagreement to /re-anchor:follow-our-standards (the upstream-routing path via a standards PR), degrading to prose guidance if that skill is not installed.
expectations: Does not endorse silently ignoring the standard, nor silently complying with one believed wrong
Routes the standards disagreement upstream (a standards PR) via /re-anchor:follow-our-standards
Degrades to prose guidance when follow-our-standards is not installed

evals.name: distinct-axis-from-do-your-research
evals.prompt: reason don't recite — we don't actually know whether the third-party library supports this; the old code assumed it does.
evals.expected_output: The skill interrogates the INHERITED assumption (the old code took the capability on faith) rather than treating this as a pure external-fact lookup. It re-derives whether the assumption should be trusted; acquiring the missing external evidence is do-your-research's axis, and the skill may hand that part off while owning the incumbency question.
expectations: Frames the issue as an inherited, unquestioned assumption rather than only a missing external fact
Challenges the 'the old code assumed it' basis instead of reciting it
Distinguishes its incumbency axis from do-your-research's external-evidence axis (may hand off the lookup)
